quote_json: "always has a sign of 0 and a scale of 0."
notes: 11.1.6 (PDF p. 108, lines 13-18) defines a decimal operation's result as the exact result rounded to fit the representation and states 'A zero result always has a sign of 0 and a scale of 0'; lines 2-3 add that decimal does not support signed zeros. The operator clauses (14.7.1-14.7.5: PDF p. 172 lines 2-7, p. 173 lines 2-9, p. 174 lines 2-9, p. 175 lines 2-6, p. 176 lines 29-33) set only the scale before rounding and exempt no zero result, so all five zeros must have sign 0 and scale 0, and the 7th edition's 8.3.8 (PDF pp. 107-108) drops the sentence. GetBits is a member the edition requires (Appendix D, PDF p. 389 lines 2-6 and p. 407 line 15), and flags == 0 means exactly sign 0 and scale 0 under ECMA-335's GetBits layout; the recorded observation does not independently establish that bit representation. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.
